dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the event grid and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The gallery calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can host a daytime gallery tour without straining my hand.
Does public-facing work itself cause trouble?
No, a normal tour is fine.
Someone new shadowed me in the programs office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the opening weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After covering alarms for a loaned sculpture overnight, I finalized the event grid at 10:30.
Could you attend a long event later?
I needed the afternoon to recover from the interrupted night.
A short committee conversation after lunch is manageable.
What keeps it manageable?
It is brief and not after a night of alarm calls.
I archived last cycle's notes on the gallery calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The recent alarm sequence has made my sleep shallow, and my packing-injury hand aches more when I am tired.
Does fatigue affect the injury?
Yes, I tense my grip and the ache becomes distracting.
A vendor call about the event grid ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the programs office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the opening weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the gallery calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Hand therapy is scheduled Thursday at 16:45, the only slot before the sculpture travels next week.
Can the therapy be moved?
No, the therapist needs to check the hand before the packing work.
I sketched next week's plan for the opening weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the event grid updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I do not drink espresso after a racing-heart episode during the last opening.
Can you push through with coffee?
No, I use a quiet walk and an earlier finish.
The donor liaison says the offsite would let me meet trustees who fund future programs.
Does that matter to you?
It matters, but I should not trade treatment for networking.
I closed the week by updating the programs office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I confirm the Thursday afternoon team retreat while I am on the artifact alarm rotation?
